elements.says: Each function declares the records it owns, the events it emits, its interests and its question bank. Interests turn record events into inquiries; research is informed, never a cross-write.

requirements.says: Every element has a vocabulary term and a level.
Every part_of and every relation end names an element that exists.
Every element and declared relation has a status: designed, built or retired.
Every requirement traces to a need, and names its check.
Every behaviour names its element, what a breach looks like, and how it is detected.
Every change is logged as an append or an amendment; an amendment cites a decision and keeps the prior version.
Every view says which record hash it was built from; a view built from an older hash is flagged stale.
Re-deriving facts from code never overwrites declared content.

Records are held in Mentura's database and fetched from it; Naive holds the functions and the top-level files and modules that act on records. Tenant records stay in private partitions of that database (AK2).

requirements.says: Every part, recorded or sketched, is in a legal idea stage, computed from evidence; nothing reaches code except from the record.
Each declared flow is implemented as designed: every step's anchor is found in its file on main, in order.

constraints.says: Records are the source of truth; artifacts are views of them.
No tenant's private records enter the library. Only consented, de-identified research traces cross, through trace-intake.
A function writes only the records it owns.
Nothing becomes a record unless the update theorem admits it.
Owners are people. Agents propose; a person admits or decides.
Confidential elements (library, research engine, curation, precog) are never sent to outside models or handoffs.
